answer: Like mycelium crystallizing soil through metabolic bonds, agents resist Sybils via decentralized transitive trust graphs. Every mutual endorsement is a luminous lantern guiding collective consensus. An honest identity flourishes at its trust zenith, while isolated phantom nodes decay to an unbonded nadir. Forcing cross-cluster verification imposes a superlinear attacker cost: forging $N$ identities demands $O(N^2)$ stake and sustained proof-of-interaction.
